newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-UKRAINE VOW TO ATTACK AGAINST GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UKRAINE VOW TO ATTACK AGAINST GERMANY.

text.p: Ukraine vowed on Wednesday to go on the attack against Germany in a World Cup qualifier in Bremen on April 30, the first major test of their calibre as group nine leaders,
Though he named 10 defenders in a provisional squad, coach Josef Sabo dismissed suggestions that his team would play defensively as "nonsense".
Sabo has selected a 29-man squad which will be reduced to 18 or 19 before the trip to Bremen.
"You can sit back for 89 minutes and still lose. You have to have a decent attack to win," Sabo said from the squad's training camp at Konche Zaspe, just outside Kiev.

He underlined the importance of being on top form against the Germans, even though Ukraine lead the group with 12 points from five matches and Germany lie only third with eight points from four matches.
"Their main qualities are well known -- discipline, team character and fitness for the whole 90 minutes," he said.
Ukraine's squad includes four newcomers. One of them, 23-year-old Yuri Benyo, has forced himself into the running just months after joining premier league side Karpati Lvov from the third division.
Sabo said he might be called on to do a close-marking job, perhaps shadowing Juergen Klinsmann.
Goalkeepers: Ilya Bliznyuk (Dnipro Dnepropetrovsk), Oleg Suslov (Cazino, Austria), Oleksandr Shovkovsky (Dynamo Kiev).

Defenders: Sergiy Bezhenar, Vladislav Vashchyuk, Oleksandr Golovko, Yuri Dmitrulin, Oleg Luzhnyi (all - Dynamo Kiev), Yuri Benyo (Karpati Lvov), Oleksandr Koval (Shakhtyor Donetsk), Ivan Pavlyukh (Dnipro), Dmitro Parfyonov (Chornomorets Odessa), Sergiy Popov (Zenit St Petersburg, Russia).

Midfielders: Viktor Skripnik (Werder, Germany), Mikhailo Starostyak, Gennady Zubov, Valery Kriventsov, Gennady Orbu (all - Shakhtyor), Andriy Gusin, Yuri Kalitvintsev, Vasil Kardash, Vitaly Kosovsky, Yuri Maksimov, Dmitro Mikhailenko (all - Dynamo), Oleksandr Kovalenko (Dnipro).
Forwards: Timerlan Guseinov (Chornomorets), Sergiy Nagornyak (Dnipro), Sergiy Rebrov, Andriy Shevchenko (all - Dynamo).
